title: Chapter 22 — Piciformes
description: Mostly tree-climbing birds with zygodactyl feet (two toes forward, two back) and stiffened tail feathers used as a prop against bark. Woodpeckers drum on resonant dead wood to establish territory and excavate nest cavities that later shelter dozens of other species — they are among the most important keystone cavity-nesters in forest ecosystems.

children.name: Picus canus
children.description: The grey-headed woodpecker, also known as the grey-faced woodpecker, is a Eurasian member of the woodpecker family, Picidae. Along with the more commonly found European green woodpecker and the Iberian green woodpecker, it is one of three closely related species found in Europe. Its distribution also stretches across large parts of the central and Eastern Palaearctic, all the way to the Pacific Ocean and south to the Himalaya and the Malay Peninsula.

It is resident across much of Europe and the western Palearctic but in Spain and Portugal it is replaced by the similar Iberian green woodpecker.

This species is described as somewhat rare, but it has a very large range and the population appears to be steady, so the International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated its conservation status as being of "least concern".

There are three described subspecies, all inhabiting various regions of southeast Africa; the red-bellied olive woodpecker, the montane olive woodpecker, and the southern olive woodpecker.

children.description: The melancholy woodpecker is a species of woodpecker. It is found in West Africa from Sierra Leone east to Nigeria, living in forests, forest edges, clearings and woodlands. It is sometimes considered to be a subspecies of the Gabon woodpecker.

children.name: Chloropicus namaquus
children.description: The bearded woodpecker (Chloropicus namaquus) is a species of bird in the family Picidae.

children.name: Chloropicus obsoletus
children.description: The brown-backed woodpecker is a species of bird in the woodpecker family Picidae. It is found in a belt across the savannah region of sub-Saharan Africa from Senegal in the west to Ethiopia, Kenya and Tanzania in the east. It is generally uncommon, but has a very large range and the population appears to be steady, so the International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated its conservation status as being of "least concern".

children.name: Chloropicus poecilolaemus
children.description: The speckle-breasted woodpecker is a species of bird in the family Picidae, which is native to sub-Saharan Africa.

children.name: Chloropicus stierlingi
children.description: Stierling's woodpecker is a species of bird in the family Picidae. It is native to Malawi, Mozambique, and Tanzania where its natural habitat is tropical dry forests in the Eastern miombo woodlands ecoregion. It is threatened by habitat destruction.

children.name: Aulacorhynchus
children.description: Green toucanets — small, green toucans found in montane forests from Mexico to Bolivia. Their bills are patterned in black, white, yellow, and chestnut. They travel in small flocks through the canopy, eating fruit and occasionally insects.

children.name: Aulacorhynchus albivittis
children.description: Found in the Andes from Venezuela to Bolivia. Green body with a distinctive white throat and a red patch at the base of the bill. Inhabits subtropical and temperate cloud forests.

children.name: Aulacorhynchus calorynchus
children.description: A toucanet with yellow eyebrow, found in the Andes.

children.name: Aulacorhynchus whitelianus
children.description: The tepui toucanet or Whitely's toucanet (Aulacorhynchus whitelianus) is a near-passerine bird in the toucan family Ramphastidae.

children.name: Pteroglossus
children.description: Aracaris — medium-sized toucans with striking plumage patterns of black, yellow, red, and green. They have serrated bills resembling a saw. More social than larger toucans, often seen in noisy flocks of up to a dozen birds. Found in lowland forests from Mexico to Argentina.

children.name: Pteroglossus inscriptus

children.name: Pteroglossus torquatus

children.name: Ramphastos
children.description: The large toucans — the iconic toucans with enormous, colourful bills that can reach half the length of the body. The bill is surprisingly light, made of keratin sheathing a honeycomb of air-filled bone. It is used for reaching fruit on thin branches, display, and thermoregulation. Found across Central and South America.

children.name: Ramphastos aurantiirostris
children.description: A toucan with orange bill, found in the Guiana Shield.

children.name: Ramphastos brevis
children.description: The Choco toucan (Ramphastos brevis) is a near-passerine bird in the family Ramphastidae, the toucans, toucanets, and aracaris.

children.name: Ramphastos toco
children.description: The toco toucan (Ramphastos toco) is a species of bird in the toucan family Ramphastidae.

children.name: Selenidera
children.description: Small toucanets with strong sexual dimorphism, found in lowland forests of South America.

children.name: Bucco
children.description: Typical puffbirds with stout bodies, large heads, and thick necks that give them a hunched, 'puffed-up' appearance. They are sit-and-wait predators, remaining motionless for long periods before sallying out to catch large insects, lizards, and other small prey.

children.name: Bucco capensis
children.description: The collared puffbird (Bucco capensis) is a species of bird in the family Bucconidae, the puffbirds, nunlets, and nunbirds.

children.name: Bucco tamatia

children.name: Bucco lymbidon
children.description: A puffbird with blue cheek from the southern Amazon.

children.name: Bucco chacuru
children.description: A puffbird with white ear patch from central and eastern South America.

children.name: Chelidoptera
children.description: A monotypic genus of unusual puffbird with a more streamlined silhouette and elongated, swallow-like wings. The Swallow-winged Puffbird is the most aerial of the puffbirds, often seen hawking insects from exposed perches in a manner reminiscent of its namesake swallows.

children.name: Hypnelus
children.description: A puffbird with two breast bands from northern South America.

children.name: Malacoptila
children.description: Medium-sized puffbirds with soft plumage from Central and South America.

children.name: Malacoptila ater

children.name: Malacoptila fulvogularis
children.description: The black-streaked puffbird is a species of near-passerine bird in the family Bucconidae, the puffbirds, nunlets, and nunbirds. It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

children.name: Malacoptila marginata
children.description: A puffbird with white whiskers from the Atlantic Forest of Brazil.

children.name: Malacoptila miniata
children.description: A puffbird with rufous breast from the Amazon.

children.name: Malacoptila mystacalis
children.description: The moustached puffbird is a species of near-passerine bird in the family Bucconidae, the puffbirds, nunlets, and nunbirds. It is one of seven species in the genus Malacoptila. It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Venezuela.

children.name: Malacoptila orbignyi
children.description: A puffbird from the western Amazon.

children.name: Malacoptila semicincta
children.description: The semicollared puffbird is a species of near-passerine bird in the family Bucconidae, the puffbirds, nunlets, and nunbirds. It is one of seven species of the genus Malacoptila. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.

children.name: Micromonacha

children.name: Micromonacha lanceolata
children.description: The lanceolated monklet (Micromonacha lanceolata) is a species of near-passerine bird in the family Bucconidae, the puffbirds, nunlets, and nunbirds.

children.name: Monasa
children.description: Black or dark grey puffbirds with a distinctive white or pale bill, known as nunbirds. They are more social than other puffbirds, often foraging in small flocks and uttering a variety of whistled and chattering calls. Their name comes from the Greek monasios, meaning solitary, though they are actually quite gregarious.

children.name: Monasa atra

children.name: Nonnula brunnea

children.name: Nonnula frontalis
children.description: The grey-cheeked nunlet is a species of near-passerine bird in the family Bucconidae, the puffbirds, nunlets, and nunbirds. It is found in Colombia and Panama.

children.name: Nonnula rubecula
children.description: The rusty-breasted nunlet is a species of near-passerine bird in the family Bucconidae, the puffbirds, nunlets, and nunbirds. It is found in Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Guyana, Paraguay, Peru, Suriname, Venezuela, and possibly French Guiana.

children.name: Nonnula ruficapilla
children.description: The rufous-capped nunlet is a species of near-passerine bird in the family Bucconidae, the puffbirds, nunlets, and nunbirds. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.

children.name: Nonnula sclateri
children.description: The fulvous-chinned nunlet is a species of near-passerine bird in the family Bucconidae, the puffbirds, nunlets, and nunbirds. It is found in Bolivia, Brazil, and Peru.

children.name: Notharchus macrorhynchos

children.name: Notharchus pectoralis

children.name: Notharchus tectus

children.name: Nyctibius ater
children.description: A black puffbird from the Amazon.

children.name: Indicator
children.description: Drably plumaged birds with a remarkable behavioural adaptation — they guide humans and honey badgers to bee nests, then feed on the exposed wax and larvae after the nest is broken open. True to their scientific name, they are living indicators of wild bee colonies. They are brood parasites, laying their eggs in the nests of barbets, woodpeckers, and other cavity-nesting birds.

children.name: Indicator indicator
children.description: The greater honeyguide (Indicator indicator) is a bird in the family Indicatoridae, paleotropical near passerine birds related to the woodpeckers.

children.name: Prodotiscus
children.description: Small, slender honeyguides with a fine, sharply pointed bill that resembles a sunbird's more than a typical honeyguide's. They are the least known and most poorly studied of the honeyguides, with a preference for forest and woodland habitats.

children.name: Prodotiscus regulorus
children.description: A honeyguide from southern Africa.

children.name: Semnornis
children.description: A small genus of barbet-like birds that form an evolutionary link between New World barbets and toucans, sharing characteristics of both groups. They have massive, brightly coloured bills like toucans but the stout body and bristled bill base of barbets. They inhabit montane forests of Central and South America.
